summary: Recorded what the target's own tests cover in this area, using the test files themselves as sources. The RestoreCommittedLogs tests (raft_test.go 1183-1279) build a single-node cluster, commit commands, snapshot, shut the node down and restart it, asserting only that the FSM is replayed up to the log store's commit index and that the commit index lies between the snapshot index and the last log index, plus a rejection case for a log store without commit tracking; none of them constructs a restart whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry and none observes the configuration or quorum the restarted node uses. The user-restore path is covered by snapshotAndRestore (raft_test.go 1633-1700), which opens a snapshot, calls Restore on the leader and asserts the FSM is reverted to the snapshot with all nodes agreeing — consistent with the repair receipt. This is a sourced observation about existing coverage, not a new gate, contract or baseline, and it changes no conclusion: the parent, constructor, split-brain and repair questions all remain explained with their defect claims, consequences, bounds and limits tied to their receipt indices, with no uncited execution and no open necessary gap. The run's remaining items are the recorded limits themselves (single harness-issued membership change, entry-count long run, harness-arranged lag for the per-node repair, self-produced snapshot for the restore, case-level rather than real-store snapshot failures for the stall, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts) rather than unanswered questions, so no further experiment is warranted within the remaining budget.
